title: Not bad enough for therapy — Nandini, 36 (USPSTF 2019)
caption:
"I'm not bad enough for therapy." US guidelines say otherwise: counseling (CBT or IPT) is recommended BEFORE crisis, not after (USPSTF, 2019).
Send this to her — and tell me, who told you to wait?
www.aiforheratx.org
#womensmentalhealth #postpartumsupport #therapyworks #maternalmentalhealth #womenshealth

scenes.text: Everyone told her to wait until it got bad. Eleven months later, it did.
phrases: Wait till it gets really bad, then go.
She waited. Nothing about waiting helped.

scenes.text: Her first therapist felt wrong, so she switched. The fit itself predicts whether therapy works.
phrases: The first one felt like a form to fill in.
She almost decided therapy wasn't for her.
She booked a different one instead.
Across ~300 studies, the bond predicts the outcome (Psychotherapy, 2018).

scenes.eyebrow: tonight, before you talk yourself out
scenes.text: Book one 15-minute consult call and ask, "Do you do CBT or IPT?" You do not have to be in crisis first.
phrases: Ask her straight: do you do CBT or IPT?
If the fit feels wrong, switch — that is allowed.
Walk 20 minutes tomorrow; WHO asks for 150 a week.
